title: kuro plugin manifest
description: Structure of a kuro content-source plugin's plugin.json. schemaVersion 1. This file is the published contract; cross-field rules a JSON Schema cannot express live in the plugin CLI and are documented in contract/plugin-api/ABI.md. Adapted from dazacode/swayve-plugins, whose manifest design this reuses rather than re-derives.

schemaVersion.description: Manifest schema version this plugin.json is written in. Currently 1.

id.description: Globally unique reverse-DNS plugin id, at least three segments. Written into stored SourceBindings, so it may never change once shipped.

name.description: Human readable name, shown in the source picker. No emoji.

description.description: One paragraph describing what this plugin adds.

license.description: SPDX licence identifier, for example Apache-2.0.

yorozoPluginApi.description: Plugin ABI level this bundle targets. See contract/plugin-api/ABI.md.

minimumYorozoVersion.description: Lowest kuro client version this plugin runs on.

platforms.description: Surfaces the plugin supports. A plugin that needs a WebView must not claim macos, windows or linux -- PlatformCapabilities.hasWebView is false there (AGENTS.md rule 10).

capabilities.description: Which ABI methods this plugin implements. The host resolves plugins by capability, never by id.

permissions.description: Host facilities the plugin may touch. An unknown entry is a load refusal, never a silent drop.

entrypoint.description: The bundle's module name inside payload/, without extension. Also the plugin's directory name and the archive's filename stem.

language.description: ISO 639-1 code for the content this source serves, or 'multi'.

network.description: Outbound network declared up front. ctx.http refuses anything not matched here, and the user sees this list before installing.

settings.description: Settings the HOST renders on the plugin's behalf, on every surface. A plugin never draws UI. A setting may choose among the hosts `network.hosts` already grants; it may never add one -- a value naming a host outside the grant is refused when it is set, and `ctx.http` refuses it again if it ever gets there.

timeouts.description: Plugin-requested timeout budget. The host still applies its own hard limits.

semver.$comment: Strict SemVer 2.0.0, the regex published at semver.org.

pluginId.$comment: Reverse-DNS, three or more lowercase segments.

assetPath.$comment: Relative, inside assets/, no traversal, no drive letter, no backslash.

hostPattern.$comment: A hostname, optionally with a single leading *. wildcard label. A bare '*' is deliberately not expressible.

capability.$comment: One per ABI method. 'search' and 'episodes' and 'resolve' are the three a usable source implements.

permission.$comment: segment-transform-js is specified at API level 1 and NOT implemented; a host must refuse a plugin that declares it (ABI.md section 4.4).

hosts.description: Every host the plugin may reach. Enforced by the host before a packet leaves, not by the SDK.

key.description: What the plugin's own code reads this setting by, when that differs from `id`. Present on a converted bundle, whose upstream preference keys are arbitrary strings while ids are not. The host stores and answers by `id`; this records the mapping so a derivation is auditable in the manifest rather than only in the converter.
